newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia cuts human rights funding in budget.
newsitem.headline: Australia cuts human rights funding in budget.

text.p: Funding cuts to Australia's Human Rights and Equal Opportunity Commission in the 1997/98 federal budget will result in the loss of 60 staff jobs, representing one third of its workforce.
The commission said the cuts, from December, will see its funding slashed to A$11 million from $A16 million over the next two years.

"At a time of great need for restating the values of inclusion, non-discrimination and tolerance in Australia, these cuts mean the commission will be unable to continue to work at its current level," said commission president Sir Ronald Wilson
in a statement. Wilson is a former justice of the High Court of Australia.
"It will have to reassess its priorities and operations as the cuts will have a significant impact on the work able to be done in the future," Wilson said.
